The test image shows a tomato field with widespread wilting — plants are collapsed/drooping across entire rows, still green but severely wilted. This is a **whole_plant** view.

From the whole_plant index, key candidates showing wilt: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight, Verticillium_Wilt, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus.

Now viewing reference images one at a time, one per class:
Bacterial_Wilt shows trellised plants wilting with some browning. Test image shows field-grown plants completely collapsed. Let me check Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.
Southern_Bacterial_Wilt shows a single plant severely wilted, green foliage drooping. Good match to the pattern. Let me check Southern_Blight.
Southern_Blight shows staked plants, less matching. Let me check Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus and Verticillium_Wilt.

Interesting - Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus whole_plant (Bugwood 1568048) shows a very similar field layout to the test image (Bugwood 1568061). Both have same hazy sky, same row arrangement, same soil color. The Bugwood numbers are nearly consecutive, suggesting the same disease documentation set. Let me check Verticillium_Wilt next.
Verticillium_Wilt shows a leaf close-up with V-shaped lesions — not matching the whole-plant field view. Now checking Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus.
TSWV shows ring spots on a leaf — not matching the field-wide wilt pattern. Now checking Late_Blight.
Late_Blight shows a leaf with brown lesions — not matching. Now my 8th view — Phytophthora_Blight.

I have now viewed 8 reference images across 8 different classes. Let me synthesize:

**Analysis:**

Test image (Bugwood 1568061): A large field of tomato plants that are collapsed/flattened across entire rows. Plants are still green but spread low to the ground with distorted growth. No obvious brown lesions visible at this scale.

Key findings from reference comparison:
- **CMV (Bugwood 1568048)**: Extremely similar — same hazy sky, same soil color, same field scale, same row arrangement. Bugwood numbers 1568048 and 1568061 are nearly consecutive, strongly suggesting they come from the same disease documentation set. CMV causes stunting, distortion, bushy low growth which matches the test image's collapsed/spread-out plant appearance.
- **Bacterial_Wilt**: Shows trellised plants wilting (different setting, plants remain more upright)
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Single plant dramatically drooping — possible match but a different scale/setting
- **Southern_Blight**: Staked plants, different visual character
- **Verticillium_Wilt, TSWV, Late_Blight, Phytophthora_Blight**: All showed leaf-level close-ups with specific lesion patterns, not matching this whole-field view

The CMV reference is the closest visual match: same field type, same environmental conditions, same scale of observation, and near-consecutive Bugwood IDs strongly indicate same disease documentation set. CMV symptoms (stunted, bushy, collapsed plants that appear lighter/distorted) also align with what the test image shows.
